LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyPacts_Tip: A truce can be offered to a people at war with the colony when it has beaten a raid of theirs in the last 15 days, holds one of their notables or kin, or a friend of both has spoken for peace; they offer one now and then after a raid of theirs is beaten. Agreed, their envoy comes to the gate under their sign of parley, vouched for by a people at peace with both, and the colony's speaker walks out to swear it; with no such people it is sworn by word. A season or a year, with a price either way. While it holds, their raiders' camp near the colony breaks up; once per truce their firebrands may raid anyway (one in ten). At its end it is a peace if their goodwill has come to 0. A pact (with a people at goodwill 20 or more, never the Empire) runs a year and can be renewed: a defense pact brings their band when the colony calls during a threat (at most once a season, nine times in ten) and asks the colony's fighters for their town when it is attacked; a trade pact brings their caravan each season and takes a cart of the colony's surplus for silver. Attacking a partner breaks it, and every people in reach hears of it. Off: nothing new is made, and those live run out by their terms.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TruceRaids: While a truce holds, the storyteller doesn't send that people's raids to that home.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_TruceRaids_Tip: A small hook on the game's choice of raiders: a people holding a truce with the home being raided isn't chosen. Raids whose people is set beforehand (quests, other mods) still come, and break the truce when they do. Needs the deeper game hooks. Off: a truce keeps only Rimfolk's own raids and camps away.
